subject: Materials Science
title: Oxidation at High Temperature
description: A quick, practical guide to Oxidation at High Temperature.

hook.text: A jet turbine blade glows at 1,100°C — oxygen attacks the metal surface far faster than at room temperature.

buildup.text: High-temperature oxidation grows a thick oxide scale — the rate follows a parabolic law as oxygen diffuses through it.

discovery.text: Chromia and alumina scales grow slowly and adhere well — they protect the metal underneath.

twist.text: Iron oxide is porous and spalls off — exposing fresh metal to oxidize again, endlessly.

climax.text: Nickel superalloys with aluminum form alumina scales that protect turbine blades at extreme temperatures.

punchline.text: At high temperature, the oxide you grow determines how long you survive.

quiz.question: Why are chromia and alumina scales protective at high temperature?
options: They grow slowly, adhere well, and block further oxygen diffusion
